title: Switchback simulation scenario
description: A complete, self-contained description of one simulation run: the fleet's behaviour model, the traffic presented to it, the events that disturb it, and what gets recorded. A scenario is data, validated against this schema, canonicalised and content-addressed (ADR-0005 §3). Nothing here is code and nothing here may read the environment: a scenario that hashes to the same bytes must produce the same bytes of trace on any machine, in any language, in any year. The acquirer *catalog* referenced by `fleet.catalog` is a separate artifact (see constraints/catalog/) and is pinned by hash, exactly as a ConstraintSet pins it.

schema_version.description: Grammar version. Bumped only by a change to this file.

id.description: Stable, unique, lowercase. Appears in every trace row and every benchmark table, so it is part of the citation of a number, not a filename.

model_version.description: The behavioural contract of the acquirer model: which random draws exist, in what order they are addressed, and what the parameters mean. Bumping this invalidates every committed benchmark number, which is the point.

seed.description: Master seed. Every random value is derived from (seed, stream key, draw index) — see ADR-0005 §4. It is an integer, never a string, so that derivation is a fixed-width integer mix in every language.

extends.description: Optional single-parent inheritance: this document is deep-merged over the named scenario, then `extends` is stripped and the RESOLVED document is what gets hashed. An extension may not change `seed` or `model_version` (SV2).

events.description: Scheduled disturbances in virtual time. Ordered by (at_s, array index) at run time; document order is not significant.

clock.description: Virtual time. The harness never sleeps: simulated latency is arithmetic on this clock, which is why a 30-day scenario can run in seconds.

start.description: UTC, 'Z' literal. No local time: a scenario that shifted with the runner's timezone would not be a scenario.

resolution_ms.description: Tick size of the virtual clock. Coarser ticks are faster and hide sub-tick ordering; 1 ms is the default and the only value a committed benchmark may use.

source.description: Where transactions come from. Synthetic: generated from `traffic`. Trace: replayed from a recording (#13's export). Both are replayable; only the second replays reality.

model.description: poisson: exponential inter-arrival draws, index-addressed so the i-th arrival is the same in any run. fixed: deterministic 1/rate spacing (faster; aliases against the diurnal pattern, so it is for micro-benchmarks only).

congestion_coefficient.description: How much of an arrival-rate increase shows up as fleet-wide latency: lat_mult *= 1 + congestion_coefficient * (rate(t)/nominal - 1). Zero means a traffic spike that slows nobody down, which is not what a traffic spike does. Model constant of fleet-v1, exposed per scenario because it is the knob that decides whether 'Black Friday' means more transactions or worse transactions.

diurnal.description: Deterministic closed-form load shape. Analytic on purpose: a diurnal pattern drawn from the PRNG would be a second, correlated source of variation nobody could predict from the document.

contextMix.description: The joint context distribution the harness samples. Keys are the fields ADR-0004's predicates read, so a scenario cannot under-specify a document the engine will be graded on.

sca_exemption_share.description: Share of SCA-applicable traffic that arrives with acceptable exemption evidence (#11 owns the estimate; the harness only needs it to generate the field).

deadline_ms.description: The request's deadline. Fixed per scenario unless a benchmark is specifically about deadline sensitivity.

weights.description: Categorical distribution. Keys are closed per field (SV7); values are non-negative and at least one is positive. Need not sum to 1 — the checker normalises, and the document stays readable.

traceSource.description: Replay of a recorded stream (#13's Parquet export). A trace supplies contexts and attempt keys; outcomes come from the same key-derived streams as a synthetic run, which is what makes a counterfactual on a real event reproducible.

path.description: Repo-relative. Absolute paths and '..' are rejected (SV9): a benchmark must run anywhere.

context_fields.description: The fields the trace actually carries. Anything absent must be modelled, and the ADR-0005 §5 finding is that the cost of an absent field is measurable and large.

catalog.description: Path to the acquirer capability/economics catalog this fleet is described against (constraints/catalog/*.json). Capability and price are catalog facts, not scenario parameters.

catalog_hash.description: Content hash of the catalog, in the same canonical form as a ConstraintSet's policy.catalog_hash. Scenario and fleet move together or the scenario does not run (SV3).

acquirers.description: Keyed by acquirer id. Keys must exist in the catalog (SV3). The KEY SET is part of the world: adding an acquirer must not perturb any other stream (measured in [M3]).

acquirer.description: The behaviour of one synthetic acquirer. Every field is a parameter of a model, never a canned answer: the engine learns these rates from data it is given, exactly as it would in production.

base_rate.description: P(issuer approves | reached, no challenge) for the reference context (consumer_credit, EEA, median ticket).

amount_sensitivity.description: Large tickets are declined more (issuer risk models) and tiny tickets slightly more too (fixed-fee economics, issuer floor rules). Two-kink linear, capped.

multipliers.description: Per-key multiplicative adjustment. Keys are closed per field (SV7).

declineMix.description: Distribution over decline codes, conditional on a decline. Weights need not sum to 1. Whether a code is RETRYABLE is a scheme fact from the catalog, not a scenario parameter (SV4) — a scenario may not declare a hard decline soft.

scheme.description: iso8583 = card authorization response codes (51, 05, 14, ...). nacha = ACH return codes (R01, R03, R12, ...). The ticket's R01/R03/R12 are nacha; the card path is iso8583. Both are supported because the scheme changes the CATALOG, not the model.

latency.description: Quantile-parameterised latency: a lognormal body fitted through (p50, p95) with a generalised-Pareto tail above p95 pinned to p99 (ADR-0005 §2). Three quantiles and a tail index, not a distribution name — the point is that a scenario author thinks in the numbers they would see on a dashboard.

floor_ms.description: Network floor: no response is faster than this. Also keeps the body model from producing sub-RTT latencies at extreme draws.

tail_index.description: Generalised-Pareto shape ξ. Higher = heavier tail. p99.9 is a MODEL OUTPUT of this parameter, not an input — see [M4], where it moves 3x between tail models that agree at p99.

threeDS.description: 3DS flow quality. `frictionless_rate` is P(no challenge | authentication attempted); the abandonment rate applies to challenged transactions and feeds the `abandoned` outcome (#11 owns the real estimates).

liability_shift_uplift.description: Multiplier on approval probability when a challenge was COMPLETED (issuer risk models approve more once authenticated). Applied to the challenged branch only.

lateSettlement.description: The 'up but slow' case (#10): an attempt the engine gave up on can still be authorized by the issuer later. The harness emits it as a scheduled event on the virtual clock, which is the only way the engine's lease logic can be tested at all.

share.description: P(the issuer's decision eventually arrives | attempt exceeded the deadline).

correlation.description: Latent factors that couple acquirers. Without them a fleet-wide event is simulated as N independent events, which is not what a processor outage looks like.

acquirers.description: Two or more members (SV8): a factor with one member is not correlation, it is a typo.

bucket_s.description: Width of the latent-factor time bucket. The factor is constant within a bucket and AR(1) across buckets.

ramp_s.description: Linear ramp from nominal to the target multipliers. Gradual is the hard case: a step change is detectable by any detector, a ramp is detectable only by one that knows what it is looking for (#8).

outage.description: A sudden failure. `failure_mode` is the whole point: an engine that handles `timeout` correctly can still be wrong about `connection_refused`, because only the first leaves the result unknown (#10).

failure_mode.description: timeout: the socket hangs past the deadline, outcome UNKNOWN. connection_refused / http_503: a fast, certain error. decline_storm: the acquirer is up and answering, but everything comes back as a soft decline — indistinguishable from the issuer, and the case a naive health model gets wrong.

auth_multiplier.description: Approval-rate multiplier during the event; only meaningful for decline_storm (a refused connection never reaches an issuer). Default 0.02.

recovery.description: What happens after degradation. A step recovery is the assumption that makes a benchmark optimistic: the arm is clean the instant the event ends, so a router that returns to it early is never punished.

tau_s.description: Time constant for the exponential curve. Required when curve == exponential (SV6).

auth_multiplier_from.description: The approval-rate multiplier the acquirer is recovering FROM. Default 1.0 = no auth effect.

latency_multiplier_from.description: The latency multiplier it is recovering from. An acquirer that comes back from an outage is slow before it is clean; stating the residual is the author's job, not the model's default (SV6).

fleetShock.description: A displacement of a latent factor: the mechanism behind 'correlated spikes' that are not any single acquirer's fault (a network event, a scheme outage, a regional DNS failure).

magnitude.description: Shift of the latent factor, in standard deviations of its stationary distribution.

mode.description: chosen_only: record the arms the policy actually called (what production can record). all_arms: record the outcome for EVERY acquirer the policy could have called (what a synthetic harness can record, and what #15's counterfactual needs). The cost difference is measured in [M7]; the bias difference is measured in [M8].

context_fields.description: Which context fields to persist. Default (absent) = all, because a field you did not record is a field you have to model later — [M8] prices that.
